My journey

It started at ten years old in my father’s machine shop, with two threaded pipes and one question: “Why?”

1 · Curiosity

My father, a mechanical engineer, explained not just how parts work but why they are designed that way. AutoCAD in 12th grade was my first step from idea to drawing.

2 · Hands-on learning

During my B.E. in Mechanical Engineering I spent breaks in industries and machine shops, running lathes and milling machines, and led the transmission team of a 4×4 SAE Baja buggy.

3 · Toward automation

Cam-follower timing systems showed me where pure mechanics stops. Combining mechanics, electronics, code and 3D printing led to a patented 5-axis printer table. Three failed prints taught me GD&T the hard way.

4 · Research

At IIT Madras I moved from building to researching, testing, validating and documenting, including a hip-implant test rig that replicates human walking.

5 · Today

Mechanical design, manufacturing, automation, simulation and analysis, with MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS, CFD and FEM.

Why does it work? Why can’t it be simpler? Why can’t we build it differently?
